content: Certain substances have been identified to interfere with the accuracy of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) devices. For example, acetaminophen, ascorbic acid (vitamin C), and hydroxyurea have been demonstrated to cause erroneous glucose readings on specific CGM systems. Consequently, it is essential for individuals using CGM devices to regularly review their medications and supplements with their healthcare provider to mitigate the risk of inaccurate readings. Table 7.4 provides a detailed list of substances that may impact CGM accuracy across various device models.
